thread:
anya: quick check — I hit a converter failure when ingesting a community model that uses a custom SentencePiece variant. Exported model works locally but runtime chokes on kv-cache offsets :confused:
priya (runtime): can you paste the error? if it's an offset mismatch it's likely a tokenizer length/offset mapping problem between export and runtime.
mike (bench): fyi, we saw similar for a weird tokenizer last quarter. benchbot flagged noncanonical token IDs during auto-smoke.
anya: stack: `RuntimeError: KVCache write out-of-bounds (idx 102400 > buffer 65536)` then a bunch of `decode()` warnings. Model is 16k context but seq len spikes when tokenizing emojis.
sam (infra): is this reproducible on dedicated? or only on on-prem staging?
anya: repros on staging (dedicated pool) and locally with same binary. ONNX export showed token length 512 -> ok, but runtime gets larger.
priya (runtime): two quick suspects: 1) tokenizer uses multi-byte sentinel tokens which our tokenizer adapter maps to multiple token IDs but runtime expects single id per token; 2) encoder produces variable-length BOS/CLS handling. We should add conversion unit test that compares tokenization length + token ids for a corpus sample.
mike (bench): adding to bench harness: run `tokenizer-parity` for N=50 inputs (mix emoji, CJK, long whitespace) and assert len(ids) and ids checksum match export. I can add perf sig test too.
anya: agree. proposal: admission checks should include: - tokenizer parity (ids + offsets) - kv-cache stress (simulate worst-case seqs with emoji/CJK) - deterministic generation smoke (seeded, 3 samples) - pinned fallback for >context if runtime mismatch
priya (runtime): +1. For tokenizer parity: we need a canonical mapping artifact saved alongside model: `tokenizer_manifest.json` with `type`, `vocab_checksum`, `special_token_map`. converter should emit it.
sam (infra): where does that live? model registry versioned object? we already store `config.json` per model. adding `tokenizer_manifest.json` is fine. ensure it's hashed into model fingerprint so admission can compare.
mike (bench): benchbot: create ticket for adding `tokenizer-parity` to pre-admit pipeline and add a CI job that runs on each model upload.
benchbot: created RED-ML-3482: "tokenizer-parity + kv-stress admission tests" and assigned to @mike.
priya (runtime): small detail: runtime adapter needs to accept both single-id and multi-id special token encodings. I can add tolerant decoding: if special token expands to multiple ids, collapse to first id for kv-indexing but keep offsets for generation. Will sketch change.
anya: API-level acceptance criteria: - no kv OOB for generated test corpus - tokenization checksum identical to converter output for 95% of corpus samples (we'll iterate if corner cases remain) - export includes `tokenizer_manifest.json` and `exporter_version`.
mike (bench): timeline? i can add tests in bench harness this week, but infra needs to accept new artifact in registry.
sam (infra): we can accept artifact. I'll add a migration to the registry schema to include `aux_artifacts` array. ETA EOD Friday.
anya: ok. next steps: priya implement runtime tolerance PR + unit tests, mike add bench CI + benchbot ticket, sam add registry schema migration. I'll follow up with a short RFC doc for converter edgecases.
priya (runtime): I'll open PR with tests by Thursday. :thumbsup:
mike (bench): will wire up bench CI and link to RED-ML-3482.
sam (infra): adding registry change to backlog, will ping infra-owners.
anya: thanks all. if anyone finds more weird tokenizers drop example payloads here or upload to /mnt/model-buckets/anon-samples. :eyes:
